q: What volume convention or particle-count assumption yields the paper's claimed 0.225 wt% AuFeNP loading? Our audit gives 0.014% (whole 20-um cell), 0.047% (13.8-um nucleus only), and 0.96% (100-nm shell around nucleus) — none within a factor of 2 of 0.225%.
basis: Section 3 spot_check.json 'wt%_audit' block: N=1e6, 4-nm OD NP (2-nm Fe2O3 core, 1-nm Au shell), rho_Au=19.32, rho_Fe2O3=5.24. Six denominator interpretations tested; all fail. This is the single hard numerical disagreement in the audit.
next_steps: (a) Open a GitHub issue on AKlapproth/MultiScale_AuNP_TOPAS asking for the exact volume denominator used to compute 0.225%. (b) Try a factor-4 reduction hypothesis: perhaps only ~2.5e5 NPs were actually placed and the 1e6 in the text is aspirational. (c) Try Au-only (not Au+Fe2O3) mass in the numerator with the 100-nm shell denominator. (d) Request the AuFeNP coordinate dump from the authors and compute wt% directly.

q: Does the reported OH enhancement of 2.05–2.23 hold up under seed randomization, or is this a single-seed artifact? The paper does not document RNG seeds for any of the 12 scenario runs.
basis: Section 5 blocker #2: no seeds pinned. With only 12 runs and reported per-species ranges as tight as OH ~0.18 span, the seed sensitivity is the dominant uncontrolled uncertainty.
next_steps: (a) When compute is available on uicgpu/Polaris, run Stage 3 alone with the authors' released code across 10 seeds at the (200 kVp, Center) point, using a pre-generated Stage-2 phase-space (or a proxy monoenergetic spectrum at ~110 keV effective). (b) Report the empirical seed spread of the OH enhancement and compare to the paper's cross-scenario spread — if seed spread >> scenario spread, the depth/energy trends in Table 3 are within noise.

q: Does the AuFeNP spatial realization (which specific 10^6 coordinates within 100 nm of the nucleus) matter for Table 3, or is it self-averaging at 10^6 NPs?
basis: Section 5 blocker #3: placement RNG not described, no coordinate file published. Chemical species killed at NP surfaces depend on which molecules encounter which NP, which depends on the exact cloud realization.
next_steps: (a) Regenerate two independent 10^6-NP clouds under the '<=100 nm of nucleus, uniform random' rule and rerun Stage 3 at one condition. (b) Quantify per-species enhancement ratio spread across realizations. (c) If spread is small (<5%), self-averaging holds and the placement-file gap is not blocking; if large, request the coordinate dump.

q: Are the Stage-1 (mouse) and Stage-2 (tumor) phase-space files essential for the Table 3 numbers, or can a Stage-3-only run with a synthetic ~110 keV kilovoltage spectrum reproduce the enhancement ratios?
basis: Section 5 blocker #6: intermediate .phsp files not published. This forces any replicator into the full multi-kJob upstream campaign for any Stage-3 perturbation.
next_steps: (a) Take a published SARRP-effective spectrum (SpekCalc 100/200 kVp) and drive Stage 3 directly without the mouse geometry. (b) Compare the resulting OH enhancement ratio to the paper's Table 3. (c) If within ~10%, the phase-space files are 'nice to have' not blocking, and the full pipeline claim is overstated; if not, they are a genuine reproducibility blocker.

q: The paper claims 'indirect SBs ≈ 2× direct SBs in every scenario' (Fig. 8/9). Is this driven predominantly by the choice of 40% OH→SB conversion probability, or does it survive parameter sweeps of that probability?
basis: Section 2 claim #2 + audit-target #2: the 40% probability is a chemistry-to-damage bridge parameter. Halving it to 20% would roughly halve indirect SBs and collapse the 2:1 ratio to 1:1.
next_steps: (a) Rerun Stage 3 at one condition with OH-to-SB probability in {20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%} and record indirect:direct SB ratio. (b) Compare to the ~2:1 claim. (c) If the 2:1 ratio is only realized at ~40%, the claim is effectively a tautology of the parameter choice; if it is stable across a wide range, it is a real mechanistic finding.
